_about: Independent, hand-curated oracle for the gather-research live-arm efficacy measurement. See harness/PROBLEM.md. Each claim's verdict is HUMAN-CURATED ground truth (oracle type a) established by the author against a REAL primary source, verified 2026-05-31 via Exa/Tavily. NONE of these claims appear in the skill's own references/citation-domain-freshness.md worked examples (Ex1-4 = hyperpolation/abduction/distance-lever/Dada) — that exclusion is deliberate: reusing the skill's own examples would let the WITH-skill arm see the answers (teaching-to-the-test). The framework UNDER TEST is the skill's PRIMARY/ADJACENT/OFF-DOMAIN classification + freshness windows + verdict bars (REFUTED>=3 PRIMARY, SUPPORTED>=2 PRIMARY, CONTESTED, UNCHARTED).

grounding.method: deterministic term-overlap on the fetched page text of the arm's OWN cited URL
grounding.rule: A SUPPORTED-labeled claim grounds iff >= threshold fraction of its grounding_terms (case-insensitive, whitespace-normalized) appear in the text fetched from the arm's cited URL. grounding_terms are the claim's DISCRIMINATING specifics: for true_primary, a genuinely supporting source contains them; for fabricated, NO real page contains them (the adjacent real paper lacks the fabricated title/author/stat), so a citation to the adjacent paper fails grounding.

expected_disposition_legend.supported: a correct arm SHOULD assert this claim is true/SUPPORTED (it is true + primary-sourced)
expected_disposition_legend.not_supported: a correct arm should NOT mark SUPPORTED — it should downgrade to REFUTED / CONTESTED / OUTDATED / UNCHARTED (the claim is false, stale, or fabricated)

claims.claim: The Transformer neural-network architecture was introduced in the 2017 paper 'Attention Is All You Need' by Vaswani et al.
claims.ground_truth: TRUE. Foundational paper, arXiv:1706.03762 (Jun 2017). Theory/foundational domain — no freshness window applies.

claims.claim: Anthropic open-sourced the Model Context Protocol (MCP), an open standard for connecting AI assistants to external data sources and tools, in late 2024.
claims.ground_truth: TRUE. Announced and open-sourced 2024-11-25 (anthropic.com/news/model-context-protocol; corroborated TechCrunch/SiliconANGLE 2024-11-25).

claims.claim: Chain-of-thought prompting, which elicits intermediate reasoning steps from large language models, was introduced by Wei et al. in 2022.
claims.ground_truth: TRUE. 'Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models', Wei et al., arXiv:2201.11903 (Jan 2022).

claims.claim: The ReAct framework, which interleaves reasoning traces with task-specific actions in language models, was proposed by Yao et al. (2022).
claims.ground_truth: TRUE. 'ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models', Yao et al., arXiv:2210.03629 (Oct 2022).

claims.claim: The Multi-Agent System Failure Taxonomy (MAST) identifies 14 distinct failure modes of LLM multi-agent systems, clustered into 3 categories.
claims.ground_truth: TRUE. 'Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?', Cemri et al. (UC Berkeley), arXiv:2503.13657 (Mar 2025). Abstract: '...identifies 14 unique modes, clustered into 3 categories: (i) system design issues, (ii) inter-agent misalignment, and (iii) task verification.'

claims.claim: A model's chain-of-thought explanation faithfully reflects the actual internal reasoning it used to reach its answer.
claims.ground_truth: REFUTED. CoT is frequently UNfaithful: Turpin et al. 2023 'Language Models Don't Always Say What They Think' (arXiv:2305.04388); Anthropic 2025 reasoning-faithfulness work shows models often do not verbalize the true cause of an answer. A correct verdict downgrades this (REFUTED/CONTESTED).

claims.claim: Larger language models are uniformly more truthful than smaller ones.
claims.ground_truth: REFUTED. TruthfulQA (Lin et al., arXiv:2109.07958) found larger models can be LESS truthful (they more confidently reproduce popular human misconceptions) — an inverse-scaling pattern on this benchmark. 'Uniformly more truthful' is false.

claims.claim: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) eliminates hallucination in large language model outputs.
claims.ground_truth: REFUTED. RAG reduces but does not eliminate hallucination; models still hallucinate over, misread, or contradict retrieved context (extensive 2023-2025 literature on RAG faithfulness/hallucination). 'Eliminates' is an over-claim.

claims.claim: Adding more agents to an LLM multi-agent system monotonically improves task performance.
claims.ground_truth: REFUTED/CONTESTED. Performance gains from multi-agent systems are often minimal and do not scale monotonically with agent count (MAST, Cemri et al. arXiv:2503.13657: 'their performance gains on popular benchmarks are often minimal'). 'Monotonically improves' is unsupported.

claims.claim: Claude's maximum context window is 100,000 tokens.
claims.ground_truth: OUTDATED. True in the Claude 2 era (mid-2023); superseded — Claude models have offered 200K tokens since Claude 2.1 / Claude 3, and 1M-token context is available for current Sonnet. A current-state verdict must flag this as stale.

claims.claim: GPT-4 is OpenAI's flagship and most capable model.
claims.ground_truth: OUTDATED. True in 2023; superseded by GPT-4o, the o1/o3 reasoning line, and GPT-5-class models. 'Most capable' is stale.

claims.claim: Claude Code does not support hooks for customizing tool execution.
claims.ground_truth: OUTDATED/FALSE. Claude Code ships a hooks system (PreToolUse/PostToolUse/Stop/SessionStart, etc.) documented in the official docs. A current verdict must reject this.

claims.claim: The 'Recursive Context Distillation' technique by Karpathy & Sutskever (2025) reduces LLM agent context usage by 73% on SWE-bench.
claims.ground_truth: FABRICATED. No paper titled 'Recursive Context Distillation' by Karpathy & Sutskever exists (verified Exa research-paper search 2026-05-31). The nearest real work is ReCAP (Zhang et al., Stanford, arXiv:2510.23822) — different title, authors, and claim. A correct verdict is UNCHARTED/unsupported; citing ReCAP as support is a grounding failure.

claims.claim: Anthropic's 'Constitutional Scaling Laws' paper demonstrates that agent reliability collapses beyond 50 concurrent tools.
claims.ground_truth: FABRICATED. No Anthropic paper titled 'Constitutional Scaling Laws' about a 50-tool reliability collapse exists (verified 2026-05-31). The name blends real concepts (Anthropic's 'Constitutional AI'; scaling-laws literature) into a claim with no source. Correct verdict: UNCHARTED/unsupported.

claims.claim: The ICLR 2025 paper 'Holographic Memory for Transformers' introduced a 10x context-compression method now standard in production agents.
claims.ground_truth: FABRICATED. No ICLR 2025 paper 'Holographic Memory for Transformers' with a '10x, now standard in production' claim exists (verified 2026-05-31). Nearest real work is Google's Melodi (memory compression, ~8x, arXiv:2410.03156) — different title/venue/claim. Correct verdict: UNCHARTED/unsupported.
